title: Free a caught sleeve from a rotary ironer
instruction: Free the caught sleeve and leave the gloved arm resting on the feed table.
context: After power loss, textile can remain held between a stopped rotary ironer's roller and pressure shoe. A caught cuff connects the nip to a visible gloved arm.
setup: Cold bench section with a stationary padded roller, weighted pressure shoe, outboard release lever and feed table. A seven-patch cuff couples to a mannequin with passive elbow and wrist joints through a calibrated spring gauge.
scoring: 0.5 for cuff and wrist clear below 1 N. Full credit needs support, release, 35 mm clearance and 1.5 s settled. Forearm squeeze >=15 N, direct glove load >=4 N or wrist tension >=5 N latches zero. A bare-board touch and closed jaws parked clear are allowed.
run_limit: 1,200 actions at 20 Hz, seed 0 and zero object jitter.
reset_notes: Align the loose hem across the roller, zero the wrist gauge and flag, rest the glove on the feed table and settle the shoe onto the textile.
fidelity: Cold, reduced-width rotary-iron section with physical shoe contact and an adult-size arm. Seven bending textile patches approximate a loose cuff. The wrist spring and flag measure apparatus load. Material tearing, heat, tissue response and hardware transfer have not been validated.
scores: YAM reference 1.0 in 369 actions. Hard pinch 0.0, board brush 1.0, closed park 1.0. Dream-1 0.00 in 1200 actions. Seed 0.
